Proposition
[constant curvature of Euclidean spheres]

Source: petersen:page-0135 ↗ prop:pet-ch4-hess-r-euclidean ↗ prop:pet-ch4-triple-vanishing-diagonalizes-operator For $n\ge 3$, the level sphere $S^{n-1}(R)\subset \mathbb {R}^n$ (with its induced metric $g_R=R^2ds_{n-1}^2$) has constant curvature $R^{-2}$.
Proof

↗ prop:pet-ch4-euclidean-sphere-constant-curvature \sketch By subsection 2.1, the second fundamental form of the level sphere is $\mathrm{II}=r^{-1}g_r$. Since the ambient curvature is zero, the Gauss equation gives

\[ \mathfrak R^\top (X,Y)Z =r^{-2}\bigl(g_r(Y,Z)X-g_r(X,Z)Y\bigr). \]

Thus section 1 applies and every bivector eigenvalue, hence every sectional curvature, equals $r^{-2}$. Put $r=R$.

□
